w10_T4_004089: Priya opened a savings account with $182 in it. A holiday bonus from her bank tripled her balance overnight. The next month she paid $166 to cover a family emergency. A matching workplace program then boosted her remaining balance to 8 times its size. She and her brother agreed to split that money in half between their two accounts. Finally, she used $973 of her half to pay off a loan. It had taken her bank 120 minutes, or two hours, to process her very first deposit. How much money, in dollars, did Priya have left after paying off the loan?
w10_T4_004095: The Sunrise Bakery started Monday morning with 185 loaves of bread on its shelves. During the morning rush, the bakers added 31 freshly baked loaves to the shelves. By afternoon, a new delivery contract meant the shelves held 5 times as many loaves as before. That evening, a citywide festival used up 929 loaves for its food stalls. Right after the festival, a grateful town council tripled what remained as a surprise restock. Later that night, the bakery donated 192 loaves to a shelter. How many loaves of bread did the Sunrise Bakery have left by the end of the night?
w10_T4_004096: Malik started Saturday morning with 163 baseball cards in his collection. By midday, a trading fair had grown his collection to 7 times its original size. In the afternoon, he traded away 889 duplicate cards to other collectors. That evening, his cousin gave him 7 more rare cards as a gift. Later that night, he donated 42 cards to his school's card-collecting club. Malik has been collecting cards for a dozen years now, ever since his grandfather gave him his first pack. How many cards did Malik have in his collection after the donation?
w10_T4_004099: Jordan started the day with 137 marbles in his bag. He lost a match against his friend Sam and had to hand over 96 marbles. Later, Jordan won the next round and got 66 marbles back from Sam. While walking home, he found 31 more marbles that had rolled under the porch. The following day he paid Sam 23 marbles to settle an old bet. That afternoon Jordan won a final game and earned 66 more marbles from Sam. Even with all the back-and-forth, Sam still liked to claim he had more marbles overall. How many marbles did Jordan end up with?
w10_T4_004102: A shipping warehouse counted 81 pallets of ceramic mugs at the start of the day, and each pallet held 8 identical crates, giving the crew the total number of crates awaiting shipment. Every one of those crates in turn held 2 mugs, giving the exact mug count for the shift. During unloading, 630 mugs were found cracked and were pulled from the total. A partner warehouse then sent a matching shipment that grew the remaining mugs to 8 times their count. An inventory clerk found 18 extra mugs overlooked in a corner and added them to the total. Finally, the store's loyalty program awarded 5 points for every mug sold, whereas her colleague Tom's stand across town only ever offered 2 points per mug, and the whole unloading process had taken 90 minutes, which the manager logged as an hour and a half. How many loyalty points did the mugs generate in total?
w10_T4_004117: Elena picked 206 tomatoes from her garden on Saturday. She sold 120 of them at the farmers market that morning. Later she gave 62 more to her neighbor for a fruit swap. She packed what remained evenly into 6 baskets and kept only one basket for herself. Of that basket, 3 tomatoes turned out to be spoiled and had to be thrown away. A local chef then offered to double whatever she had left in exchange for helping at his restaurant. Her friend Marcus, who had grown far fewer tomatoes that season, joked that he'd never catch up to her total. How many tomatoes did Elena end up with?
w10_T4_004134: The Riverside Library shelf started the week with 162 mystery novels. By Tuesday, 82 of them had been checked out by readers. On Wednesday, 48 previously borrowed novels were returned to the shelf. On Thursday the librarian split the shelf's novels in half, moving one half into the archive room and leaving the rest on display. Friday morning, 10 water-damaged copies were pulled and discarded. That afternoon, a publisher delivered 78 brand-new novels for the shelf. Finally, a retiring teacher donated 49 more novels from her personal collection, even though the library building itself is over 500 square meters. How many mystery novels were on the display shelf by the end of the week?
w10_T4_004135: Diego began his gaming tournament run with a score of 23 points early in the morning. During the morning matches, he earned 76 additional points from quick victories. By afternoon, a bonus multiplier round doubled his entire score. In the evening session, he picked up 42 more points from a side quest. Later that night, a penalty for a rule violation cost him 131 points. Right before the tournament closed, a final loyalty bonus tripled whatever score he had left. What was Diego's final score at the end of the tournament?
w10_T4_004137: The Miller orchard started Monday morning with 207 apples in the collection bin. During the morning harvest, 94 apples were pulled out and sent to the cider press. By midday, workers added 19 more freshly picked apples to the bin. In the afternoon, half of the bin's apples were moved to a separate crate for the farmer's market. Later that evening, a neighbor dropped off 6 apples from her own tree. Just before closing for the night, the orchard added 43 more apples gathered from a late round of picking. How many apples were left in the collection bin at the end of the night?
w10_T4_004139: Oliver had 104 arcade tickets in his pouch after his first hour of games. He gave half of them to his younger sister so she could play too. He then fed the rest into a bonus machine that paid out 5 tickets for every ticket inserted. Along the way, he found 38 extra tickets someone had dropped near the prize counter. His grandfather added 34 more tickets as a birthday treat. A prize booth later ran a special offering 4 tickets for every one he turned in. Oliver then spent 223 tickets on a stuffed bear from the prize counter. How many tickets did Oliver have left after buying the bear?
w10_T4_004166: A water station's storage tank held 240 liters at the start of Monday morning. During the morning refill, an automated pump increased the tank's contents to 4 times its original amount. By afternoon, technicians split that water evenly across 4 identical tanks and kept only one tank's share for testing. In the evening, a new well connection increased that remaining amount to 7 times its size as pressure built up. Later that night, workers added 32 liters collected from rainwater, then another 30 liters pumped in from a backup tank, and finally 14 more liters topped it off. Filling the very first tank that morning had taken 180 minutes, which the site log recorded as three hours. How many liters of water were in the tested tank by the end of the night?
w10_T4_004167: Mia had 32 stickers in her album before the school fair. At the fair's mystery-pack booth, her sticker count grew to 4 times its size after she won a grand prize pack. She then traded away 26 stickers to complete a friend's collection. Afterward, she split her remaining stickers in half with her friend Leo, who already had a much bigger album than hers. She lost 15 stickers when a page fell out of her album on the bus. She then split what was left in half again, giving half to her cousin. The school fair itself lasted 6 hours from start to finish. How many stickers did Mia have left?
w10_T4_004169: Farmer Ana collected a dozen eggs from the henhouse first thing Monday morning. Later that morning, 8 of the eggs cracked while being moved to the kitchen. At midday, she used 1 more egg to test a recipe before lunch. In the afternoon, 2 eggs were set aside for a neighbor who stopped by. By evening, a new batch of hens had laid 41 more eggs, which were added to her count. How many eggs did Farmer Ana have by the end of the evening?
w10_T4_004176: The camera club printed 103 photos for its Saturday exhibit setup in the morning. By afternoon, a bulk-printing discount let them print 7 times as many photos as they'd started with. That evening, a member donated 38 extra photos from an old field trip. Later that night, the club combined every batch with eight other clubs' identical collections, growing the total to 9 times its evening size for the joint city-wide show. Just before midnight, the organizers added 54 last-minute submissions that arrived by email. The exhibit hall itself can seat 300 visitors at a time. How many photos were in the final combined collection?
w10_T4_004178: A downtown parking garage had 56 cars parked when it opened Monday morning. By mid-morning, 16 of those cars had left for work meetings nearby. Throughout the afternoon, 79 more cars pulled in as shoppers arrived at the mall next door. In the early evening, another 15 cars parked for a concert down the street. By closing time that night, 107 cars had driven out to head home. The garage has 4 separate entrances for drivers to use. How many cars were left in the garage when it closed for the night?
w10_T4_004194: A toy distributor received 151 pallets of miniature cars on Monday morning. Each pallet contained 4 crates, and workers spent the morning logging that count. Every crate held 4 boxes, which the afternoon shift catalogued next. Each of those boxes in turn contained 8 miniature cars, giving the true count of individual toys by early evening. Later that evening, a quality inspection removed 10343 toys found to have paint defects. Just before the warehouse closed for the night, workers added 8 replacement toys that had been sitting in a repair bin. Logging the very first pallet that morning had taken 240 minutes, which the shift supervisor recorded as 4 hours. How many miniature cars remained by the end of the night?
w10_T4_004196: Zoe set up her lemonade stand with 15 cups already poured that morning. A scout troop's bulk order right after opening grew her poured cups to 6 times the morning amount. Through the afternoon rush, customers bought 76 of those cups. In the early evening she mixed a fresh batch, adding 36 more cups to her stock. A caterer's order shortly after left her with 7 times as many cups as before. Just before closing, she found 6 extra cups behind the cooler and 10 more that a neighbor lent her, capping off a stand she has now run for a dozen summers. Setting up that very first batch had taken 20 minutes, which felt to her like a third of an hour well spent, though the stand's tip jar has room for 200 coins. How many cups did Zoe have at closing?
w10_T4_004199: Carlos had 152 dollars in his wallet at the start of the day. During the morning, he spent 39 dollars on groceries. By midday, he received 40 dollars back as a refund for a returned item. In the afternoon, he paid 121 dollars toward a phone bill. That evening, a friend repaid him 13 dollars he was owed. Just before bed, he spent another 36 dollars on a late dinner, even though the restaurant was only a 5-minute walk from his apartment. How much money did Carlos have left in his wallet by the end of the night?
w10_T4_004200: A plant nursery had 186 tomato seedlings ready for sale on Friday. Over the weekend, the nursery started 41 more seedlings from a fresh batch of seeds. The following week, another 46 seedlings sprouted successfully from a second tray. A supplier then delivered 21 additional seedlings to restock the shelves. Later, the nursery sold 160 seedlings to a local landscaping company. The nursery owner has been growing plants for a dozen years, ever since watering her first tray took nearly 120 minutes, which she still remembers as a full two hours of work. How many tomato seedlings did the nursery have left?
w10_T4_004203: Nina had 106 points in the school reading challenge. After finishing three more books that week, she earned 33 additional points. A bonus weekend then doubled her entire point total. She lost 168 points when a mix-up in the record system wiped out some of her entries. After the error was partly corrected, she still had to forfeit 82 more points for a late submission. Her classmate Tara, who had a much smaller total all along, ended up passing her in the rankings anyway. How many points did Nina have after the penalty?
w10_T4_004209: The school charity jar held 202 dollars at the start of the fundraiser. On the first day, the jar's coins were miscounted and 23 dollars had to be removed from the total after a recount. The next day, students donated 64 more dollars during the morning assembly. On day three, a bake sale added 36 dollars to the jar. A local business then matched part of the donations with 63 more dollars. Finally, a surprise raffle contributed another 58 dollars, though the raffle tickets themselves had been printed in a run of 500. Two organizers, Priya and Sam, noticed that Priya's personal collection can had far more coins in it than Sam's. How much money was in the charity jar after the raffle donation?
w10_T4_004212: A grocery store's rice storage held 56 kilograms at the start of Monday morning. By mid-morning, half of that rice had been sold off to a wholesale buyer, leaving only the remaining half in storage. In the afternoon, a delivery truck dropped off 14 more kilograms. Later that afternoon, another supplier brought in 75 additional kilograms. That evening, a supply agreement brought the store's rice total to 7 times what it had been. Just before locking up for the night, the store shipped out 782 kilograms to a partner branch across town, even though that branch is only 3 kilometers away. How many kilograms of rice were left in storage after the shipment?
w10_T4_004216: A stationery shop had 196 notebooks on its shelves at the start of the month. A supplier delivered 17 more notebooks the following week. A school bulk-order then took 175 notebooks off the shelves. A few days later, 25 notebooks were returned as damaged and removed from stock. Near the end of the month, a new shipment added 67 notebooks to the shelves. A holiday sale then brought in enough customers that the shop's remaining stock needed to be replenished to 4 times its size to meet demand, a demand the owner hadn't seen in a dozen years of running the shop. How many notebooks were on the shelves after the restock?
w10_T4_004217: Jake's fitness tracker showed 111 flights of stairs climbed at the start of the charity stair-climb event on Saturday morning. By late morning, he had climbed 41 more flights during the first relay. In the early afternoon, he added another 49 flights while pacing his friend Ravi, who was climbing far fewer flights overall. By late afternoon, he'd tackled 77 more flights in a final push before the break. That evening, the event organizers synced everyone's trackers with a team bonus, crediting Jake with 6 times his flight count for the team leaderboard. Just before the event closed for the night, a last bonus lap added 59 more flights to his team total. Jake has taken part in this event for a dozen years running. How many flights of stairs did Jake's team total show at the end of the night?
w10_T4_004226: A small food truck business had 148 dollars in its account after a slow start to the season. A viral social media post then brought in enough new customers that the account balance grew to 9 times its earlier amount. The owner paid 293 dollars to restock ingredients for the following week. A catering client then paid an extra 19 dollars as a tip. Regular weekend sales added 63 dollars more to the account. A costly refrigerator repair cost the business 896 dollars. Finally, a franchise partner made an investment that brought the account balance to 4 times its size. How much money was in the food truck's account after the investment?
